note.text: An opinion states a view; a reason explains why the speaker holds it. An example makes the reason concrete. In a club discussion, acknowledge another view before responding and distinguish a preference from a checked fact. I prefer drama does not prove every pupil should choose it. Spoken discussion needs turn-taking and attentive listening; here you prepare the wording and read an original dialogue before practising with a partner.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original dialogue: Bih says, I prefer the reading club because I enjoy discussing stories. Ayuk replies, I see your point, but the environmental club interests me because members organise useful projects. Bih asks, Could the clubs share an exhibition? They propose a joint activity instead of treating preferences as an argument about personal worth.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Build a turn from view, reason and example. Use I agree because or I see your point, but rather than repeating yes or no without explanation. Do not invent membership figures or activities for a real school. Use the fictional club in the model or information the teacher confirms.
